slides.title: Cleany PromoFlow
slides.subtitle: Put promotion investment behind profitable, executable plans

notes.purpose: Open at executive altitude and establish the decision outcome.
notes.talk_track: Cleany has an opportunity to connect promotion performance, forward demand, commercial events, and inventory feasibility in one governed planning journey.
evidence: Customer and product data in the demonstration are synthetic.
The solution is running in the Cleany PromoFlow demonstration environment.
notes.transition: Introduce the people in the room and their decision roles.
notes.likely_question: What decision does this solution improve?

slides.title: Introductions
columns:
Filipe Deo
Field Engineering
Solution architecture and demonstration

Jeff — VP Revenue Growth Management
Sarah — VP Supply Chain
Trevor — Promotion Planner
Emily — Supply Planner

notes.purpose: Make roles and interests explicit before discussing the solution.
notes.talk_track: Filipe will facilitate the discussion and demonstration. Jeff is focused on profitable growth, Sarah on availability and inventory efficiency, Trevor on scenario planning and approval, and Emily on feasibility inputs and execution alignment.
evidence: Personas reflect the intended cross-functional buying and operating group.
notes.transition: Set expectations for the call with a concise agenda.
notes.likely_question: Who owns the final promotion decision?

slides.title: Today’s discussion
columns:
1  Business outcomes
What should improve and how we measure it

2  Decision journey
How data and AI connect the workflow

3  Live demonstration
From portfolio attention to approval

4  Pilot proposal
Scope, measures, and next decision

notes.purpose: Give both executive and domain stakeholders a clear meeting contract.
notes.talk_track: We will align on outcomes first, then show the connected decision journey, demonstrate the workflow, and finish with a measurable pilot proposal.
evidence: Agenda intentionally leads with outcomes rather than architecture.
notes.transition: Lead with the quantified opportunity and distinguish potential from realized value.
notes.likely_question: How much time is allocated to the demonstration?

slides.title: $642K modeled margin opportunity — $267K is already supply-ready

notes.purpose: Anchor the discussion on the modeled value pool and executable subset.
notes.talk_track: Across 204 profitable modeled opportunities, the current value pool represents about $642K in expected incremental margin. Ninety-three READY opportunities represent $267K. These are modeled opportunities, not booked savings.
evidence: 204 profitable modeled opportunities in planner_opportunities.
$642,397 modeled incremental margin across all profitable opportunities.
$267,100 modeled incremental margin across 93 READY opportunities.
notes.transition: Explain why Cleany cannot consistently capture that value today.

slides.title: The promotion decision is fragmented
columns: Past performance, mechanics, ROI, and events are analyzed separately.
Scenario creation and approval cross multiple systems and spreadsheets.
Inventory and receipt constraints are often discovered after commercial commitment.

notes.purpose: Frame a specific CPG planning problem rather than a generic data challenge.
notes.talk_track: The issue is not a lack of data; it is the separation of commercial evidence, planning workflow, and availability context at the moment of decision.
evidence: Synthetic source contracts represent POS, TPM, ERP/MDM, WMS, IBP/OMS, and commercial-calendar feeds.
notes.transition: Show the outcome scorecard that connects the problem to buyer KPIs.
notes.likely_question: Which existing system does PromoFlow replace?

notes.purpose: Present current decision workload, executable opportunity, and historical exposure in one view.
notes.talk_track: The operational view currently has 18 submitted or pending items and 22 plans requiring availability review. The opportunity pool includes $267K of READY modeled margin. Historical promotions with lost sales recorded $3.0M of revenue at risk.
evidence: Live Overview endpoint: 51 upcoming records, 18 submitted/pending, 22 at risk.
Historical promotion_explorer: $3,005,912 revenue at risk across 217 promotions.
Modeled future values are potential, not realized savings.
notes.transition: Define exactly how improvement will be measured after rollout.

slides.title: Measure realized impact, not modeled promise
columns:
Approval cycle time
Share of plans reviewed before commitment
READY opportunity conversion
Forecast error and override rate

Incremental margin and trade ROI
Revenue at risk from lost sales
Availability at event start
Planner hours saved

notes.purpose: Establish a credible measurement method and avoid relabeling predictions as savings.
notes.talk_track: The model creates a prioritized value pool. Realized value is measured after execution against prior cycles and, where possible, matched non-pilot promotions. We separate workflow adoption, forecast quality, and commercial outcomes.
evidence: Historical portfolio ROI baseline is 2.38x.
Historical revenue-at-risk baseline is $3.0M for promotions with lost sales.
No causal claim is made from observational uplift.
notes.transition: Move from the scorecard into the connected decision journey.
notes.likely_question: How will you attribute improvement to PromoFlow?

slides.title: From fragmented planning to one governed decision journey

notes.purpose: Create a visual transition from business outcomes to solution and demonstration.
notes.talk_track: The solution connects evidence, prediction, feasibility, and human approval without hiding the underlying economics.
evidence: The implemented workflow spans Lakeflow, Unity Catalog, MLflow, Lakebase, Unity Gateway, Genie, and Databricks Apps.
notes.transition: Describe the solution in three business-relevant layers.

slides.title: One platform, three responsibilities
columns:
Lakeflow ingests enterprise feeds
Unity Catalog governs data and AI

MLflow scores opportunities
Genie answers portfolio questions

Lakebase serves plans and decisions
Databricks Apps guides human approval

notes.purpose: Explain the architecture without turning the presentation into a feature tour.
notes.talk_track: The lakehouse is the governed analytical record, AI prioritizes and explains opportunities, and Lakebase plus the app provide the transactional decision experience.
evidence: 1,200 historical promotions, 48 imported TPM plans, and 204 opportunities materialized.
Unity Gateway generates narratives from governed scenario facts.
Reverse Lakehouse Sync is intentionally outside the demonstrated scope.
notes.transition: Show exactly what will be demonstrated in the application.
notes.likely_question: Why do we need both the lakehouse and Lakebase?

slides.title: Live demonstration: tell, show, decide
slides.body:
Overview — prioritize approvals, risk, and uncovered events
Past Promotion Analysis — learn from margin, ROI, uplift, and lost sales
Upcoming Promotions — inspect readiness, receipts, and shortfalls
Opportunity Inbox — identify event-aligned value pools
Scenario Studio — compare governed alternatives side by side
Decision Workspace — approve and generate a governed AI brief
Genie — ask the same governed data in natural language

notes.purpose: Set up the demonstration before opening the application.
notes.talk_track: I will follow one story: identify the portfolio priority, learn from history, inspect an upcoming plan, create and compare a scenario, approve it with availability context, and ask a follow-up question through Genie.
evidence: Databricks App deployment is RUNNING, ACTIVE, and SUCCEEDED.
Authenticated endpoints return 1,200 history rows, 51 upcoming records, and 204 opportunities.
notes.transition: After the demo, summarize the current operational portfolio that the workflow exposes.
notes.likely_question: Can users filter by recognizable product and market names?

notes.purpose: Land the demonstration with the size of the decision queue and risk exposure.
notes.talk_track: The combined operational view includes imported plans and app-authored scenarios. It provides a single queue for what is upcoming, awaiting approval, and constrained.
evidence: 28 of 51 current records are approved.
Six plans combine no planned receipt with a projected shortfall.
One upcoming commercial event is not yet covered by a plan.
notes.transition: Connect forward planning to the historical evidence base.
notes.likely_question: Why are these counts higher than the imported TPM plan counts?

slides.title: Historical evidence sets the baseline
columns:
$3.0M
Revenue at risk from lost sales

notes.purpose: Show the historical baseline used to learn patterns and measure future improvement.
notes.talk_track: The history demonstrates scale and gives us a baseline for economics and availability exposure. The 24.4 percent average uplift is observational. We will not claim it as causal incrementality.
evidence: 1,200 historical promotions.
$71,533,009 incremental margin and $30,027,677 trade spend.
217 promotions recorded 321,696 lost units and $3,005,912 revenue at risk.
notes.transition: Translate the baseline and value pool into a controlled pilot scorecard.

slides.title: Proposed pilot: prove value in one planning cycle
columns:
One category
Two retail clusters
One commercial event window
RGM, promotion, supply, and data owners

Approval cycle time
READY opportunity conversion
Realized incremental margin and ROI
Forecast error and revenue-at-risk reduction

notes.purpose: Propose a bounded next step with measurable commercial and operational outcomes.
notes.talk_track: Start small enough to learn quickly but large enough to include the full decision journey. Agree the baseline and measurement protocol before the first recommendation is approved.
evidence: The prototype already supports category, product, market, event, approval, and readiness filters.
Historical and forward metrics are available at promotion and opportunity level.
notes.transition: Close with the decision requested from the customer team.
notes.likely_question: How long would the pilot take?

slides.title: Confirm the pilot category, clusters, owners, and baseline measures

notes.purpose: End with a specific, low-friction customer decision.
notes.talk_track: The requested next step is to nominate the pilot scope and owners, then validate source mappings and baseline measures in a working session.
evidence: The demonstration uses synthetic data; production onboarding begins with source-contract and KPI validation.
notes.transition: Open the discussion for business and technical questions.
notes.likely_question: What do you need from Cleany to start?
